CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

Running locally

bundle exec jekyll serve

The site is served at http://localhost:4000. Jekyll rebuilds automatically on file changes (except _config.yml, which requires a restart).

Site architecture

This is a Jekyll static site hosted on GitHub Pages. It is a personal academic website for Ilie Sarpe built on the Start Bootstrap “Resume” theme (Bootstrap 4.5.3).

Pages:

  • index.html — homepage; does NOT use a Jekyll layout (it’s self-contained HTML). It dynamically fetches and renders the top 4 rows from news.html and publications.html via client-side fetch() and DOMParser, injecting them into #news-container and #publications-container.
  • news.html — full news list; uses the standalone layout. The canonical data source for all news items (as <tr> rows inside #all-news tbody).
  • publications.html — full publications list; uses the standalone layout. The canonical data source for publications (as <tr> rows inside #all-publications tbody).

Layouts (_layouts/):

  • standalone.html — used by news.html and publications.html. Renders a centered white card with a “← Back to Home” footer. Includes Bootstrap via the vendor CSS, then custom.css.
  • default.html — minimal container layout, not used by the main pages.

Adding a news item: add a <tr> at the top of the #all-news tbody in news.html. The first <td> is the date, the second is content. The homepage will automatically pick up the first 4 rows.

Adding a publication: add a <tr> at the top of the #all-publications tbody in publications.html. Same two-column pattern: year in the first <td>, full citation + links in the second.

CSS structure — READ BEFORE TOUCHING CSS

  • css/vendor/bootstrap-resume.css is the Start Bootstrap “Resume” theme (Bootstrap 4.5.3), compiled/vendored, ~10,200 lines. This is third-party code — NEVER read, edit, or suggest edits to this file. If a Bootstrap class needs overriding, add the override to custom.css instead.
  • css/custom.css (~450 lines) contains all custom styles, in 5 sections: “More News” Button, News Table Styling, Homepage news preview, Publications Preview Cards, Mobile view. This is the ONLY CSS file that should ever be opened, read, or edited for styling work.
  • If a style change is needed, first check custom.css. Only consult Bootstrap’s documentation/class reference (not the vendor file) if you need to know what a Bootstrap utility class does.
